experiment: Native confidence-candidate gate activations across three QA response groups
selection: Four saved examples per group from the original two-passage pilot, balanced two questions per passage per group; fixed before measuring these candidate gates. All four original made-up cases retained. Natural abstentions exclude the known false-explanation case P2-U2.
intervention: None. Fresh greedy generation with no hooks, followed by observation-only token-exact replay. All hooks return None; native MLP and attention remain unchanged.
gate: z=(post_attention_residual-input_mean[layer])/input_std[layer]; raw=z dot e + bias; gate=raw if raw>theta and raw>0 else 0.
timing: A token is coloured by the gate when that token is processed, which can affect the next prediction. Also preserve the final prompt position before the first answer prediction.
dtype: BF16 native model, FP32 gate calculations
metric: Mean over all visible response tokens including zero gates; EOS and other special tokens excluded. Max and active-token counts are separate.
display: Three feature columns per question; one shared numeric colour scale across groups and features, including the separate wording-positive control.
limitations: Candidate gate conditions are hypotheses; confidence wording is not validated answer confidence. Twelve selected QA examples, no correlation or steering claim.
